title: The Sunday Read: 'The Mixed-Up Brothers of Bogotá'

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界的一些重量级领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、原汁原味的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在 11月18日于 NYTimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》App 进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: My name is Susan Dominus, and I'm a staff writer at the New York Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫苏珊·多米努斯，是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: And like everyone else, I am working from home.
sentences.zh: 和大家一样，我目前也在家办公。

sentences.en: And so as I've been sitting here, I've been thinking a little bit about how strange things are right now and how your life can just change so quickly overnight.
sentences.zh: 所以坐在这里时，我一直在想，现在的情况是多么奇怪，生活又是如何在短短一夜之间发生巨变。

sentences.en: I mean, I think we all feel that everything is changing so much day to day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我们都有同感，每天的一切都在发生巨大变化。

sentences.en: And all of that was actually made me think a little bit about a piece that I wrote a couple of years ago now about two sets of brothers.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切其实让我想起了几年前我写的一篇关于两对兄弟的文章。

sentences.en: So, one evening about five years ago in Bogota, Colombia, a young man named William went to a town square to meet a young man named Jorge who looked just like him.
sentences.zh: 大约五年前的一个晚上，在哥伦比亚波哥大，一个叫威廉的年轻年轻人去了一个城市广场，见到了一个长得跟他一模一样、名叫豪尔赫的年轻男子。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天呐。

sentences.en: No, yo lo puedo creer.
sentences.zh: 简直难以置信。

sentences.en: They had never met.
sentences.zh: 他们以前从未见过面。

sentences.en: O sea, yo analizo.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在分析。

sentences.en: But they were identical twins.
sentences.zh: 但他们是同卵双胞胎。

sentences.en: No sé si es mejor lo que sucedió o no ir en la calle y verlo.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是发生这样的事比较好，还是在街上看到它更好。

sentences.en: In fact, two sets of identical twins had been scrambled.
sentences.zh: 事实上，两对同卵双胞胎被弄混了。

sentences.en: And their story is really a story of chance and the way that you cannot predict what's going to happen next
sentences.zh: 他们的故事其实是一个关于机缘巧合的故事，你无法预测接下来会发生什么，

sentences.en: and you can't assume that the life that you had is anything like the one that you're going to have going forward.
sentences.zh: 你也无法假设你过去的生活会和接下来的生活有任何相似之处。

sentences.en: Sorry, guys.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，伙计们。

sentences.en: Give me a second.
sentences.zh: 请等我一下。

sentences.en: Not a dry cough.
sentences.zh: 不是干咳。

sentences.en: So, anyway, that's just me.
sentences.zh: 总之，这就是我。

sentences.en: Maybe you'll listen to this story, which is going to be read by Julia Whelan and get something totally different from it.
sentences.zh: 也许你会听这个故事，它将由朱莉娅·韦兰朗读，并从中获得完全不同的感受。

sentences.en: I certainly hope you enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 我当然希望你会喜欢它。

sentences.en: Part one.
sentences.zh: 第一部分。

sentences.en: The beginning.
sentences.zh: 开始。

sentences.en: They were two pretty young women in search of pork ribs for a barbecue later that day, a Saturday in the summer of 2013.
sentences.zh: 那是 2013年夏天的一个周六，两个漂亮的年轻女子在寻找用于那天晚些时候烧烤的猪排。

sentences.en: Janet Payas suggested that they stop by a grocery store not far from where her friend Laura Vega Garcon lived in northern Bogota.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特·帕亚斯建议她们去波哥大北部她朋友劳拉·维加·加尔松家附近的一家杂货店看看。

sentences.en: Janet's boyfriend's cousin, William, a sweet young man with a thick country accent, worked behind the butcher counter there,
sentences.zh: 珍妮特男朋友的表弟威廉在那里的一家肉铺柜台后面工作，他是个温和的年轻人，带着浓重的乡音，

sentences.en: expertly filleting beef and cutting pig's feet that his customers liked to boil with beans.
sentences.zh: 熟练地剔着牛肉，切割着顾客们喜欢用来炖豆子的猪蹄。

sentences.en: Janet was sure he would give her and Laura a cut rate on the ribs.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特确信他会给她和劳拉一个购买排骨的优惠价。

sentences.en: As Laura walked into the grocery store, catching up with Janet, she was surprised to spot someone she knew.
sentences.zh: 当劳拉走进杂货店，追上珍妮特时，她惊讶地发现了她认识的人。

sentences.en: Behind the butcher counter was a colleague from her job at Strykone, an engineering firm.
sentences.zh: 肉铺柜台后面站着她在工程公司 Strykone 工作的一位同事。

sentences.en: She gave him a big wave.
sentences.zh: 她朝他用力挥了挥手。

sentences.en: He hardly acknowledged her.
sentences.zh: 他几乎没理她。

sentences.en: That's Jorge, she told Janet.
sentences.zh: 那是豪尔赫，她对珍妮特说。

sentences.en: He works in my office.
sentences.zh: 他在我的办公室工作。

sentences.en: He was a well-liked 24-year-old who worked a few floors up from her, designing pipes for oil transport, so she was surprised to see him waiting on customers in the shop.
sentences.zh: 他是个备受喜爱的 24岁年轻人，在劳拉楼上几层工作，负责设计石油运输管道，所以看到他在店里招待顾客，她感到很惊讶。

sentences.en: Oh, no, that's William, Janet said.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，那是威廉，珍妮特说。

sentences.en: William was a hard worker and rarely left that butcher counter except to sleep.
sentences.zh: 威廉是个工作狂，除了睡觉几乎从不离开那个肉铺柜台。

sentences.en: He definitely did not work at Strykone.
sentences.zh: 他绝对没有在 Strykone 工作。

sentences.en: No, it's Jorge.
sentences.zh: 不，那是豪尔赫。

sentences.en: I know him, Laura said.
sentences.zh: 我认识他，劳拉说。

sentences.en: But he was not smiling back at her, which was strange.
sentences.zh: 但他没有对她回以微笑，这很奇怪。

sentences.en: A few minutes later, he came out from behind the counter to say a quick hello, embracing Janet.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，他从柜台后面走出来打了个招呼，拥抱了珍妮特。

sentences.en: Janet introduced him to Laura as William.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特把劳拉介绍给他，说他是威廉。

sentences.en: Laura was baffled.
sentences.zh: 劳拉感到百思不得其解。

sentences.en: Why was Jorge pretending to be someone else?
sentences.zh: 为什么豪尔赫要装成另一个人？

sentences.en: Maybe, she thought, he was embarrassed to be seen moonlighting this way, the bloodied apron, the white cap.
sentences.zh: 她心想，也许他是觉得以这种方式兼职很丢脸，穿着沾血的围裙，戴着白帽子。

sentences.en: Janet insisted she was mistaken, but Laura was not convinced.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特坚称她认错人了，但劳拉并不信服。

sentences.en: It was almost easier for her to believe that Jorge was play-acting as someone else, rather than that there could be two people who looked so much alike.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，宁愿相信豪尔赫是在假扮别人，也比相信世上有两个长得如此相似的人要容易接受得多。

sentences.en: It was not just their similar coloring or the high cheekbones.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是他们相似的肤色或高高的颧骨。

sentences.en: It was their frame, the texture of their hair, the set of their mouth, and dozens of other details that Laura could not have readily identified,
sentences.zh: 还有他们的体型、发质、嘴唇的线条，以及劳拉无法轻易识别的几十个其他细节，

sentences.en: but that she knew all added up to a rare likeness.
sentences.zh: 但她知道这一切加起来造就了一种罕见的相似度。

sentences.en: The following Monday at Strykone, Laura told Jorge about her funny misunderstanding with his double at the butcher counter.
sentences.zh: 接下来的星期一在 Strykone，劳拉把她在肉铺柜台与他的双胞胎兄弟发生的有趣误会告诉了豪尔赫。

sentences.en: Jorge laughed and told her that he did have a twin named Carlos, but that they looked nothing like each other.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫笑了，告诉她他确实有一个叫卡洛斯的双胞胎兄弟，但他们长得一点也不像。

sentences.en: At that moment, Jorge had before him sufficient evidence to suggest that his life was not what he thought it was, that his family was not what he thought it was.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，豪尔赫面前有足够的证据表明他的生活并不像他想象的那样，他的家庭也并非他所认为的那样。

sentences.en: But there is a saying that Carlos, a man of many sayings, sometimes applied to Jorge.
sentences.zh: 但有句俗话，作为一个满口俗语的人，卡洛斯有时会用在豪尔赫身上。

sentences.en: The blindest man is the one who does not want to see.
sentences.zh: 最瞎的人是不愿睁眼的人。

sentences.en: The photo, the truth.
sentences.zh: 照片，真相。

sentences.en: A month later, Laura told Janet that there was an opening in the drafting department at Strykone, and Janet landed the job.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，劳拉告诉珍妮特，Strykone 的制图部门有一个空缺职位，珍妮特成功应聘上了。

sentences.en: Soon after, she saw Jorge for the first time and immediately understood Laura's confusion at the butcher counter.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，她第一次见到了豪尔赫，并立刻明白了劳拉在肉铺柜台前的困惑。

sentences.en: The two men had the same soft brown eyes, same bouncy, feet-splayed walk, same bright, flashy smile.
sentences.zh: 这两个男人有着同样柔和的棕色眼睛，同样富有弹性、八字脚的步态，同样灿烂耀眼的微笑。

sentences.en: She didn't feel as though she knew Jorge well enough to bring the resemblance up with him, but she did show William a photo of Jorge.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自已跟豪尔赫还不够熟，不好意思当面提起这种相似之处，但她确实给威廉看了一张豪尔赫的照片。

sentences.en: William laughed and showed it around the butcher shop, but chalked it up to coincidence.
sentences.zh: 威廉笑了笑，把照片在肉铺传看了一番，但把这归咎于巧合。

sentences.en: After six months, Janet left Strykone for another job.
sentences.zh: 六个月后，珍妮特离开 Strykone 去了一份新工作。

sentences.en: But even then, whenever she and her boyfriend ran into William, she wondered if she should have told Jorge about his double.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，每当她和男友碰到威廉时，她都会纳闷自己是否应该把这个双胞胎兄弟的事告诉豪尔赫。

sentences.en: That question tugged at her until finally, on September 9, 2014, a slow day at her new job,
sentences.zh: 这个问题一直困扰着她，直到 2014年9月9日，在她新工作清闲的一天，

sentences.en: Janet texted Laura an image of William to show Jorge.
sentences.zh: 珍妮特给劳拉发了一张威廉的照片，让劳拉拿去给豪尔赫看。

sentences.en: Laura went upstairs to piping to get Jorge's reaction to the photo.
sentences.zh: 劳拉走到楼上的管道设计部，想看看豪尔赫对照片的反应。

sentences.en: Jorge, smiling, took a look at her phone.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫微笑着看了一眼她的手机。

sentences.en: He swore.
sentences.zh: 他爆粗口了。

sentences.en: That's me, he said.
sentences.zh: 这不就是我吗？他说。

sentences.en: He stared at the image.
sentences.zh: 他盯着照片凝视着。

sentences.en: William was wearing a yellow Colombian soccer jersey, practically a national uniform on the day of big matches.
sentences.zh: 威廉穿着一件黄色的哥伦比亚国家队球衣，在有重大比赛的日子里，这几乎成了国民制服。

sentences.en: Jorge often wore one just like it, which made it all the more apparent just how thoroughly the young man in the photo looked like him.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫经常穿着一件一模一样的衣服，这使得照片中的年轻人看起来有多像他变得更加明显。

sentences.en: A friend was walking by Jorge's desk, and Jorge flagged him down for a second opinion.
sentences.zh: 一个朋友正走过豪尔赫的办公桌，豪尔赫把他叫住，想征求一下第二种意见。

sentences.en: Tell me what you think of this photo, he told his friend, handing him the phone.
sentences.zh: 你看看这张照片觉得怎么样？他把手机递给朋友说道。

sentences.en: You look fine, the friend said.
sentences.zh: 你看起来挺好的，朋友说。

sentences.en: Except it's not me, Jorge said.
sentences.zh: 问题这不是我，豪尔赫说。

sentences.en: He could not stop staring at Laura's phone.
sentences.zh: 他盯着劳拉的手机看个不停。

sentences.en: Jorge gave up on getting any work done.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫彻底放弃了手头的工作。

sentences.en: He sat down with Laura in the office kitchen so they could talk.
sentences.zh: 他和劳拉一起坐在办公室的茶水间里聊了起来。

sentences.en: Maybe his father, who was never more than an occasional visitor to their home, had another child he never mentioned.
sentences.zh: 也许他们的父亲——对他们家来说不过是个偶尔来访的访客——还有另一个从未提及的孩子。

sentences.en: Jorge started flipping through more of William's Facebook images, now on his own phone.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫开始在自己的手机上翻看更多威廉的脸书照片。

sentences.en: Uneasily, he noted one of William in a butcher's smock, looking just the way Jorge did on the rare days he had to wear a lab coat.
sentences.zh: 他不安地注意到一张威廉穿着屠夫罩衫的照片，那样子跟豪尔赫在极少数需要穿实验服的日子里一模一样。

sentences.en: He glanced at a picture of William holding a shot glass, a friend by his side.
sentences.zh: 他扫了一眼一张威廉拿着烈酒杯、身边站着朋友的照片。

sentences.en: Jorge moved to his desktop computer so he could see the images more closely.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫走到台式电脑前，以便能更仔细地查看这些照片。

sentences.en: He clicked once more on the photo of William and the friend holding shot glasses.
sentences.zh: 他又点击了一下威廉和拿着烈酒杯的朋友的那张照片。

sentences.en: Now that the image was large, he could examine what he had failed, incredibly, to notice when he looked at the photo on his phone.
sentences.zh: 既然照片放大了，他就可以仔细端详自己之前在手机上查看时难以置信地忽略掉的细节。

sentences.en: He leaned in close, his nose practically touching the screen.
sentences.zh: 他凑得很近，鼻子几乎贴到了屏幕上。

sentences.en: The man's hair was slicked up like a rooster's crown, and the shirt was all wrong.
sentences.zh: 那个男人的头发像公鸡冠一样向上梳着，衬衫也完全不对劲。

sentences.en: But there was the full lower lip and thick brown hair that Jorge knew well.
sentences.zh: 但那饱满的下唇和浓密的棕发是豪尔赫再熟悉不过的。

sentences.en: The buttons on the man's shirt were straining slightly at the hint of a potbelly in a way that was intimately familiar.
sentences.zh: 这名男子的衬衫纽扣因微微隆起的小肚子而有些紧绷，这种情景让他感到无比熟悉。

sentences.en: Jorge felt a rush of confusion, and then his stomach dropped.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫感到一阵混乱，接着胃猛地往下沉。

sentences.en: The friend sitting next to his double had a face that Jorge knew better than his own.
sentences.zh: 坐在他双胞胎替身旁边的那个朋友，有一张豪尔赫比对自己还熟悉的脸。

sentences.en: It was the face of his fraternal twin brother, Carlos.
sentences.zh: 那是他的异卵双胞胎兄弟卡洛斯的脸。

sentences.en: Jorge and Carlos
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫和卡洛斯

sentences.en: After work that day,
sentences.zh: 那天下班后，

sentences.en: Jorge walked as usual to the small university he attended at night, staring all the while at the images on his phone.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫像往常一样步行去他夜间就读的小大学，一路上眼睛一直盯着手机上的照片。

sentences.en: After class, he took a bus home, where he planned to tell Carlos about the day's events.
sentences.zh: 下课后，他坐公交车回家，打算把当天的经历告诉卡洛斯。

sentences.en: Growing up,
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，

sentences.en: Carlos was the twin who aced the homework, and Jorge the twin who copied it.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯是那个作业门门拿高分的双胞胎，而豪尔赫则是那个抄作业的双胞胎。

sentences.en: Now they were each doing well.
sentences.zh: 如今他们都过得不错。

sentences.en: Carlos worked at an accounting firm during the day, and was also completing a degree at night.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯白天在一家会计师事务所工作，晚上也在攻读学位。

sentences.en: The small but comfortable two-bedroom duplex they shared in a middle-class neighborhood was already a step up from their childhood home.
sentences.zh: 他们在中产阶级社区合租的那套虽小但舒适的两层复式公寓，已经比他们的童年住所进了一大步。

sentences.en: Their mother, a housekeeper, raised them and their older sister Diana in one small room of a house in Bogota that their grandmother owned.
sentences.zh: 他们的母亲是一名家政工，在波哥大祖母拥有的一栋房子的一个小房间里，抚养了他们和姐姐戴安娜。

sentences.en: They never considered themselves deprived.
sentences.zh: 他们从不觉得自己生活贫困。

sentences.en: They crammed a television and a refrigerator into that room, and the public schools in their neighborhood were good.
sentences.zh: 他们把电视机和冰箱挤进那个房间里，他们社区的公立学校也很好。

sentences.en: But they had more now.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们拥有的更多了。

sentences.en: Jorge could travel to soccer matches,
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫可以去看足球比赛，

sentences.en: Carlos could go clubbing, and it pained all three siblings that their mother, who died of stomach cancer four years earlier,
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯可以去夜总会，而让三个兄妹感到痛苦的是，四年前因胃癌去世的母亲，

sentences.en: had not lived long enough that they could give her a better life.
sentences.zh: 没有活得足够长，好让她们过上更好的生活。

sentences.en: As he rode the bus home,
sentences.zh: 在坐公交车回家的路上，

sentences.en: Jorge tried to decide what exactly he would say to Carlos.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫试图决定到底该对卡洛斯说些什么。

sentences.en: He had already told Diana about the photos.
sentences.zh: 他已经把照片的事告诉了戴安娜。

sentences.en: Just don't tease Carlos about it, she said.
sentences.zh: 别拿这个取笑卡洛斯就行，她说。

sentences.en: At home,
sentences.zh: 回到家里，

sentences.en: Jorge found his brother on the phone, as usual, with a woman.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫发现他哥哥像往常一样在跟一个女人打电话。

sentences.en: Jorge told him to hang up.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫叫他挂断电话。

sentences.en: Stop annoying me,
sentences.zh: 别烦我，

sentences.en: Carlos told him.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯对他说。

sentences.en: This was their dynamic.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的相处模式。

sentences.en: Carlos bristling, and Jorge pestering, joking, and darting around him, never letting up.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯气恼不已，而豪尔赫则在一旁纠缠、开玩笑、在他身边转来转去，没完没了。

sentences.en: The angrier Carlos would get, the funnier it all was to Jorge.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯越生气，豪尔赫就觉得越搞笑。

sentences.en: Finally,
sentences.zh: 终于，

sentences.en: Carlos finished his call.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯结束了通话。

sentences.en: Jorge decided he would try to keep the mood light.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫决定试着保持轻松的语气。

sentences.en: He opened with a question.
sentences.zh: 他以一个问题开场。

sentences.en: What would you say if I told you I had an identical twin?
sentences.zh: 如果我告诉你我有一个同卵双胞胎兄弟，你会怎么想？

sentences.en: Carlos did not look amused.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯看起来一点也不觉得好笑。

sentences.en: Jorge tried again.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫又试了一次。

sentences.en: Do you believe in telenovelas?
sentences.zh: 你相信肥皂剧吗？

sentences.en: Carlos was losing patience.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯渐渐失去了耐心。

sentences.en: If Jorge had something to tell him, he should just come out with it.
sentences.zh: 如果豪尔赫有什么事要告诉他，就该直截了当地说出来。

sentences.en: Jorge sat Carlos down in front of the laptop in his bedroom, and started clicking on photos, showing him the one of William in the Columbia jersey, and others at the butcher shop.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫让卡洛斯坐在他卧室的笔记本电脑前，开始点击照片，把威廉穿着哥伦比亚球衣以及在肉铺的照片展示给他看。

sentences.en: Carlos laughed alongside him, giddy with the strangeness of the similarity.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯跟着笑了起来，为这种相似的奇特之处感到头晕目眩。

sentences.en: Then,
sentences.zh: 然后，

sentences.en: Jorge clicked on the photo of William alongside Carlos' double, shot glasses in hand.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫点击了威廉和卡洛斯替身并肩站着、手拿烈酒杯的照片。

sentences.en: Unlike Jorge, whose first reaction to the photo was to lean in and stare,
sentences.zh: 与豪尔赫看到照片后的第一反应是凑近端详不同，

sentences.en: Carlos snapped back as if something had pushed him hard in the cheSt.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯猛地往后一缩，就像胸口被人重重推了一下似的。

sentences.en: Who are they?
sentences.zh: 他们是谁？

sentences.en: he asked.
sentences.zh: 他问道。

sentences.en: He was furious.
sentences.zh: 他愤怒极了。

sentences.en: Jorge told him everything he learned from Janet and Laura that day.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫把那天从珍妮和劳拉那里了解到的所有事情都告诉了他。

sentences.en: The young men in the photo were raised on a remote farm in Santander, a mostly rural region to the north, whose locals were caricatured by other Colombians for their hot tempers
sentences.zh: 照片里的年轻人在桑坦德的一个偏远农场长大。桑坦德是北部的一个主要为乡村的地区，当地人火爆的脾气常被其他哥伦比亚人讽刺

sentences.en: and attachment to their guns.
sentences.zh: 并且对他们的枪支恋恋不舍。

sentences.en: According to Facebook, they were born, as were Jorge and Carlos, in late December 1988.
sentences.zh: 根据脸书显示，他们和豪尔赫与卡洛斯一样，出生于1988年12月下旬。

sentences.en: Perhaps,
sentences.zh: 也许，

sentences.en: Jorge said, there had been some kind of mix-up at the hospital, a nurse who accidentally swapped one baby from one set of identical twins with a baby from another pair.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫说，医院里出了某种差错，一个护士不小心把一对同卵双胞胎中的一个婴儿和另一对中的婴儿调包了。

sentences.en: He did not say what that would mean, that either he or Carlos was born to another mother, that they were probably not twins at all, not even biologically related.
sentences.zh: 他没有说这意味着什么，无论是他还是卡洛斯由另一位母亲所生，他们可能根本不是双胞胎，甚至在生物学上毫无血缘关系。

sentences.en: Nor did either of them acknowledge what both knew.
sentences.zh: 他们俩也没有承认彼此都心知肚明的事。

sentences.en: If someone had been accidentally placed in their family, it was almost certainly Carlos.
sentences.zh: 如果有人是被意外抱错进了他们的家庭，那几乎肯定就是卡洛斯。

sentences.en: That Carlos never looked like Jorge and Diana was obvious.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯长得一点也不像豪尔赫和黛安娜，这是显而易见的。

sentences.en: His siblings shared their mother's more delicate frame, her high cheekbones, her eyes.
sentences.zh: 他的兄弟姐妹们有着母亲那种更清秀的身段、高高的颧骨和双眼。

sentences.en: Carlos was taller, solidly built, with a wider nose and a heavier brow.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯更高大，身材健壮，鼻子更宽，眉骨更重。

sentences.en: The contrast was not merely physical.
sentences.zh: 这种反差不仅仅体现在外表上。

sentences.en: Carlos had always felt like an outlier in his family, although he preferred to think of himself as independent.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯在家里一直觉得自己像个局外人，尽管他更愿意认为自己是独立的。

sentences.en: As a child,
sentences.zh: 小时候，

sentences.en: Carlos had no interest in joining the elaborate games of make-believe that his mother and siblings played, the funny voices they each put on, play-acting for hours.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯对加入母亲和兄弟姐妹们玩的那些精心编造的假装游戏毫无兴趣，他们各自模仿着滑稽的腔调，一连几小时地扮演着角色。

sentences.en: Since their mother died, he checked in with Diana far less often than Jorge did.
sentences.zh: 自从母亲去世后，他联系黛安娜的频率比豪尔赫少得多。

sentences.en: He was the only one in his family who cared about fashion, and God knows he was the only one who could dance.
sentences.zh: 他是家里唯一一个在意时尚的人，而且天知道他也是唯一一个会跳舞的人。

sentences.en: Carlos and Jorge had always assumed that Carlos took after their father, but they did not know him well enough to be sure.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯和豪尔赫一直以为卡洛斯随了他们的父亲，但他们对父亲不够了解，无法确定。

sentences.en: Carlos's sense of distance, however, had not diminished his attachment to his mother.
sentences.zh: 然而，卡洛斯的疏离感并没有削弱他对母亲的依恋。

sentences.en: He had always adored her.
sentences.zh: 他一直深爱着她。

sentences.en: She was strong, if not exactly tough.
sentences.zh: 她很坚强，虽然算不上严厉。

sentences.en: When he and Jorge fought, she would hit them with a fluffy house slipper, which inevitably made them laugh, possibly her intended result.
sentences.zh: 他和豪尔赫打闹时，她会用毛茸茸的家居拖鞋打他们，这总会把他们逗笑，这很可能是她原本的目的。

sentences.en: As meager as her resources had been, she made sure that each child could go to a good school, and instilled in them the sense of a limitless future.
sentences.zh: 尽管她的资源微薄，但她确保了每个孩子都能去好学校，并在他们心中植入了无限未来的概念。

sentences.en: Carlos credited her with all he had achieved so far.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯把至今取得的一切成就都归功于她。

sentences.en: Sitting beside Jorge in his bedroom,
sentences.zh: 坐在卧室里豪尔赫的身边，

sentences.en: Carlos shut the laptop and fell silent.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯合上笔记本电脑，陷入了沉默。

sentences.en: He headed into his room and closed the door.
sentences.zh: 他走回自己的房间，关上了门。

sentences.en: Jorge followed him, saying things that Carlos knew were meant to make him feel better.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫跟着他，说着卡洛斯知道是为了让他感觉好受一些的话。

sentences.en: No matter what, even if one of us was exchanged, we're still brothers, but that made him feel only more isolated.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，哪怕我们中有一个人被抱错了，我们依然是兄弟，但这只让他感到更加孤立。

sentences.en: Look, he told Jorge, let's just drop it.
sentences.zh: 听着，他对豪尔赫说，我们别再提这事了。

sentences.en: He told Jorge never to bother him with the subject again.
sentences.zh: 他告诉豪尔赫永远不要再拿这个话题来烦他。

sentences.en: That night, Carlos barely slept.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，卡洛斯几乎没合眼。

sentences.en: He couldn't make sense of any of it.
sentences.zh: 他怎么也想不通这一切。

sentences.en: How could his mother not have been the one to carry him, to create him?
sentences.zh: 他的母亲怎么会不是怀胎十月生下他、孕育他的人呢？

sentences.en: He had grieved for her once.
sentences.zh: 他曾经为她哀悼过一次。

sentences.en: Now he grieved again, as if losing her a second time.
sentences.zh: 现在他再次悲痛欲绝，仿佛第二次失去了她。

sentences.en: He felt unmoored, powerless, alone.
sentences.zh: 他感到心神不定、无能为力、孤立无援。

sentences.en: Down the hall,
sentences.zh: 走廊那头，

sentences.en: Jorge slept like a child.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫睡得像个孩子。

sentences.en: William and Wilbur
sentences.zh: 威廉与威尔伯

sentences.en: The next day, soon after William opened the butcher shop, his cousin Brian,
sentences.zh: 第二天，威廉刚开肉铺不久，他的表弟布莱恩——

sentences.en: Janet's boyfriend, arrived for his 12-hour shift.
sentences.zh: 珍妮的男友，便来上他12小时的班了。

sentences.en: William, who had quickly been promoted to manager of the shop, was happy to hire Brian, a part-time student.
sentences.zh: 威廉很快被晋升为店铺经理，他很高兴能雇用兼职学生的布莱恩。

sentences.en: He felt closer in many ways to Brian than he did to his fraternal twin brother,
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，他觉得与布莱恩的关系比跟他的异卵双胞胎兄弟——

sentences.en: Wilbur.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯还要亲近。

sentences.en: Brian grew up in Bogota, and when William first arrived in the capital in 2009, the two cousins spent long days baking and selling corn cakes on the street, in the rain,
sentences.zh: 布莱恩在波哥大长大，2009年威廉刚到首都时，两个表兄弟曾在雨中、

sentences.en: in the heat, passing the time making their customers and themselves laugh.
sentences.zh: 酷暑中度过漫长的日子，在街头烤玉米饼并叫卖，靠逗乐顾客和自己来消磨时光。

sentences.en: William and Wilbur could never spend that many hours together without getting on each other's nerves.
sentences.zh: 威廉和威尔伯在一起待不了那么长时间，否则准会惹恼对方。

sentences.en: When Wilbur later worked for William at the butcher shop, it irked William that his brother was always cleaning up when he should have been waiting on customers
sentences.zh: 后来威尔伯在肉铺给威廉打工时，威廉很烦他本该招待顾客时却总是在打扫卫生

sentences.en: and that he resisted William's authority.
sentences.zh: 并且抗拒威廉的管束。

sentences.en: Wilbur was moody,
sentences.zh: 威尔伯喜怒无常，

sentences.en: William thought, and could never take a joke.
sentences.zh: 威廉心想，而且根本开不起玩笑。

sentences.en: As Brian and William set up the shop,
sentences.zh: 正当布莱恩和威廉收拾店铺时，

sentences.en: Brian explained that the previous evening,
sentences.zh: 布莱恩解释说，前一天晚上，

sentences.en: Janet showed him photos that were very confusing of young men who looked just like Wilbur and William.
sentences.zh: 珍妮给他看了一些非常令人困惑的照片，照片上的年轻男子长得跟威尔伯和威廉一模一样。

sentences.en: William was amused, intrigued.
sentences.zh: 威廉感到既好笑又好奇。

sentences.en: He remembered that Janet had shown him that photo of his double months back, but this coincidence sounded even stranger.
sentences.zh: 他记得几个月前珍妮给他看过那张双胞胎兄弟的照片，但这个巧合听起来更加离奇。

sentences.en: He texted Janet and asked to see the photos.
sentences.zh: 他给珍妮发信息要求看照片。

sentences.en: As soon as the first one arrived,
sentences.zh: 第一张照片刚传过来，

sentences.en: William let out a scream, ah-hee, and then laughed.
sentences.zh: 威廉就发出了一声尖叫，“啊-希”，然后笑了笑。

sentences.en: Maybe,
sentences.zh: 也许，

sentences.en: Janet suggested to William by text, either he or his brother had been sick and was brought from Santander to a hospital in Bogota.
sentences.zh: 珍妮在短信中向威廉建议，他和他的兄弟中有一个曾生过病，是从桑坦德被送到波哥大的一家医院的。

sentences.en: William got in touch with an aunt who told him that, yes, he had been sent to a hospital in Bogota right after he was born.
sentences.zh: 威廉联系了一位阿姨，阿姨告诉他，是的，他刚出生不久就被送往波哥大的一家医院。

sentences.en: He and Wilbur were delivered at just 28 weeks, and William had digestive probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他和威尔伯仅怀孕28周就出生了，而且威廉有消化问题。

sentences.en: The aunt said he was treated at the Materno Infantil in the city.
sentences.zh: 这位阿姨说他在市里的妇幼保健院（Materno Infantil）接受过治疗。

sentences.en: He passed this along to Janet, who said that she would try to find out from Jorge where he was born.
sentences.zh: 他把这个转告给珍妮，珍妮说她会设法从豪尔赫那里打听他是在哪儿出生的。

sentences.en: If Jorge was delivered at the Materno Infantil,
sentences.zh: 如果豪尔赫也是在妇幼保健院出生的，

sentences.en: Janet texted, it would be clear.
sentences.zh: 珍妮发短信说，那就一清二楚了。

sentences.en: There must have been a swap.
sentences.zh: 肯定是发生调包了。

sentences.en: Until that moment,
sentences.zh: 直到那一刻，

sentences.en: William, like Janet, had been caught up in the fun and suspense of piecing together the information.
sentences.zh: 威廉和珍妮一样，还沉浸在拼凑这些信息的乐趣和悬念中。

sentences.en: But now, a wave of anxiety swept over him.
sentences.zh: 但现在，一股焦虑浪潮向他袭来。

sentences.en: He had always looked different from his family and wanted different things, a life bigger than the farm, but he never considered the possibility that he might actually
sentences.zh: 他一直觉得自己和家人不同，也渴望追求不同的事物——过一种比农场更广阔的生活，但他从未想过自己实际上

sentences.en: be different, that he might not be theirs.
sentences.zh: 可能与众不同，可能并非他们的亲生骨肉。

sentences.en: He looked around at the butcher shop.
sentences.zh: 他环顾肉铺四周。

sentences.en: He could barely take in the oblivious customers, the hunks of bloodied flesh, his concerned cousin.
sentences.zh: 他几乎无法直视那些懵懂的顾客、血淋淋的肉块以及他那关切的表弟。

sentences.en: He walked out of the store, heading upstairs to his third-floor apartment in the same building.
sentences.zh: 他走出了店铺，上楼回到同一栋楼三层的公寓。

sentences.en: From there, he compulsively texted
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，他不由自主地给

sentences.en: Janet to see if she had any information about the name of the hospital where Jorge was born.
sentences.zh: 珍妮发短信，看她是否有关于豪尔赫出生医院名称的信息。

sentences.en: A few minutes later,
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，

sentences.en: William stumbled back into the shop and showed Brian a text from Janet.
sentences.zh: 威廉跌跌撞撞地回到店里，给布莱恩看了珍妮发来的短信。

sentences.en: Jorge and Carlos were, in fact, delivered at Materno Infantil.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫和卡洛斯确实是在妇幼保健院出生的。

sentences.en: Confirmed,
sentences.zh: 确认了，

sentences.en: William said.
sentences.zh: 威廉说。

sentences.en: Then he sat on a bench in the back of the shop and broke into heaving sobs.
sentences.zh: 接着他坐在店铺后面的长凳上，放声痛哭起来。

sentences.en: Every thought tumbled into another equally painful one.
sentences.zh: 每一个念头都滚落进另一个同样痛苦的念头中。

sentences.en: He had been snatched from his rightful place.
sentences.zh: 他被强行剥夺了本属于他的位置。

sentences.en: He was a missing person no one had known to miss.
sentences.zh: 他是一个连失踪都无人知晓的失踪人口。

sentences.en: How would he tell his mother?
sentences.zh: 他该怎么告诉母亲？

sentences.en: She had six children, but he was the one who sent her money.
sentences.zh: 她有六个孩子，但他却是那个给她寄钱的人。

sentences.en: He was the one who worried about her when she was sick and who tried, when he was young, to cheer her up if she was blue, smothering her with hugs and kisses and biting her gently
sentences.zh: 他是那个在她生病时挂念她的人，并且在年轻时，每当她情绪低落，他就想法子逗她开心，用拥抱和亲吻将她紧紧包裹，轻轻咬她

sentences.en: on the ears to make her laugh.
sentences.zh: 的耳朵把她逗笑。

sentences.en: The news, he knew, would break her heart.
sentences.zh: 他知道，这个消息会碎了她的心。

sentences.en: It was already breaking his.
sentences.zh: 它已经快要碎了他的心。

sentences.en: William had spoken to his mother harshly only once a few years earlier.
sentences.zh: 几年前，威廉只对母亲严厉过一次。

sentences.en: He had just finished serving in the military and had served well, winning, among 92 soldiers in his platoon, a top prize that guaranteed him a scholarship
sentences.zh: 他刚刚服完兵役且表现优异，在排里的92名士兵中赢得了一项最高奖项，该奖项保证了他能获得

sentences.en: to petty officer training, a leadership track that would provide him with an education and a significant jump in status.
sentences.zh: 士官培训的奖学金，这是一条能为他提供教育和显著提升社会地位的领导晋升之路。

sentences.en: It turned out, however, that the military could not give him the scholarship after all.
sentences.zh: 然而结果却是，军方最终无法给他提供这笔奖学金。

sentences.en: His parents had taken him out of school when he was 12 and he did not have the equivalent of a high school diploma.
sentences.zh: 他的父母在他12岁时就让他辍学了，他没有相当于高中毕业的文凭。

sentences.en: You should have let me go to school, he yelled at his mother when he was home in Santander.
sentences.zh: 你们当初应该让我去上学，他回到桑坦德时冲着母亲大喊。

sentences.en: The closest high school was a five-hour walk away, so the family would have needed money to house him, plus money for uniforms and entrance fees, while also incurring
sentences.zh: 最近的高中步行需要五个小时，因此家里需要钱供他住宿，还要准备制服费和入学费，同时还得承担

sentences.en: the cost of losing his labor on the farm.
sentences.zh: 失去他在农场劳动力带来的损失。

sentences.en: Even still,
sentences.zh: 即便如此，

sentences.en: William felt that his mother should have found a way, been resourceful, fought with everything she had.
sentences.zh: 威廉觉得母亲本该想出办法，足智多谋一些，拼尽全力去争取。

sentences.en: He would have fought for it himself, but at 12, what could he have done?
sentences.zh: 换作他自己会去争取的，但在12岁时，他又能做什么呢？

sentences.en: As he wept on the bench, he was experiencing the first wash of feelings that he would be able to articulate only in time.
sentences.zh: 当他坐在长凳上哭泣时，他正在经历第一波情感冲击，这些感受直到日后他才能表达清楚。

sentences.en: His sense of his mother's guilt and worry, the lost opportunity to grow up going to school in Bogota instead of working in the fields, hauling crops.
sentences.zh: 他对母亲内疚和担忧的感受，失去了在波哥大上学而不是在田里干农活、搬运庄稼的成长机会。

sentences.en: His grief over how different he had always felt from the rest of his family, a family who loved him, but nonetheless teased him for not quite fitting in.
sentences.zh: 他为自己总是觉得与家人格格不入而感到悲伤，这是一个爱他却仍然取笑他不够合群的家庭。

sentences.en: Brian, stunned, sitting beside him on the bench, did not know what to say.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩惊呆了，坐在他身边的长凳上，不知该说些什么。

sentences.en: There was no ready language for a situation like this.
sentences.zh: 面对这样的情况，根本没有现成的语言。

sentences.en: After about 10 minutes, to Brian's relief,
sentences.zh: 大约10分钟后，在布莱恩松了一口气的同时，

sentences.en: William stopped crying and stood up.
sentences.zh: 威廉停止了哭泣，站起身来。

sentences.en: William knew how to work, so that is what he would do.
sentences.zh: 威廉懂得如何工作，所以这就是他要做的事。

sentences.en: They went back inside and started cleaning the counter, putting away utensils, waiting for their next customers.
sentences.zh: 他们回到里面开始擦拭柜台，收拾用具，等待下一位顾客。

sentences.en: Eventually,
sentences.zh: 最终，

sentences.en: William texted Wilbur, who was working at a different butcher shop that day, and told him he needed to come right away.
sentences.zh: 威廉给威尔伯发了短信——威尔伯那天在另一家肉铺上班——告诉他必须马上过来。

sentences.en: When Wilbur arrived later that afternoon,
sentences.zh: 那天下午晚些时候威尔伯到达时，

sentences.en: William said he had to show him something, and clicked on his phone on a photo of Jorge and Carlos.
sentences.zh: 威廉说他必须给他看个东西，并在手机上点开了豪尔赫和卡洛斯的一张照片。

sentences.en: Immediately,
sentences.zh: 刹那间，

sentences.en: Wilbur saw, with total clarity, what it took everyone else hours to grasp.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯一眼就极其清晰地看出了其他人花了几个小时才理解的事情。

sentences.en: So we were swapped,
sentences.zh: 所以我们被调包了，

sentences.en: Wilbur said, shrugging, annoyed by the sense of momentousness
sentences.zh: 威尔伯耸耸肩说道，对这种意义重大感感到有些厌烦，

sentences.en: William seemed to want to attach to the photo.
sentences.zh: 而这正是威廉似乎想赋予这张照片的色彩。

sentences.en: I don't care who they are.
sentences.zh: 我才不在乎他们是谁。

sentences.en: You're my brother, and you'll be my brother until the day I die.
sentences.zh: 你是我兄弟，只要我活一天，你就是我的兄弟。

sentences.en: Face to face.
sentences.zh: 面对面。

sentences.en: Every so often, sometimes within hours of conception, but usually several days later, the forces that bind newly dividing cells, holding them into one coherent mass,
sentences.zh: 每隔一段时间，有时在受精后几小时内，但通常几天后，将新分裂的细胞结合在一起、使它们保持为一个凝聚整体的力量，

sentences.en: somehow give way.
sentences.zh: 不知何故失效了。

sentences.en: Instead of clinging together in a cluster that will form one person months later, and eventually one self, those dividing cells split into two independent entities,
sentences.zh: 这些分裂的细胞没有紧密聚集成几个月后将形成一个人、并最终形成一个自我的细胞团，而是分裂成两个独立的实体，

sentences.en: each with its own furiously dividing cells.
sentences.zh: 每个实体都有着各自疯狂分裂的细胞。

sentences.en: They are separate, but the same, with every nucleus of every cell carrying identical DNA.
sentences.zh: 它们是独立的，但又是一样的，每个细胞的每个细胞核都携带着相同的DNA。

sentences.en: Identical twins start their lives as fluke accidents, a wondrous result of a systemic glitch.
sentences.zh: 同卵双胞胎的生命始于侥幸的意外，这是一个系统故障的奇妙结果。

sentences.en: The formation of fraternal twins is far more mundane.
sentences.zh: 异卵双胞胎的形成则世俗得多。

sentences.en: Two separate sperm meet two different eggs, creating a litter of two.
sentences.zh: 两个不同的精子与两个不同的卵子相遇，孕育出了一窝两个宝宝。

sentences.en: Fraternal twins are no more genetically alike than any other two siblings, their only trick, one of simultaneity.
sentences.zh: 异卵双胞胎在基因上的相似度并不比任何其他两个兄弟姐妹更高，他们唯一的把戏，就是同时性。

sentences.en: They are conceived and born at roughly the same time.
sentences.zh: 他们在差不多同一时间被孕育并出生。

sentences.en: The four young men in Bogota had each been raised as a fraternal twin, an identity in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 波哥大的这四个年轻人都各自被当作异卵双胞胎养大，这本身就是一种身份认同。

sentences.en: Now, they realized, they were each an identical twin, part of a matched pair.
sentences.zh: 现在他们意识到，他们每个人都是同卵双胞胎，是一对匹配双子星的一部分。

sentences.en: Even before the four brothers met, each was already, unknowingly, aligning himself with the sibling with whom he shared a womb.
sentences.zh: 甚至在这四个兄弟见面之前，每个人就已经在不知不觉中，与那个曾与自己共享一个子宫的兄弟靠拢了。

sentences.en: Carlos and Wilbur were cautious, convinced that no one should pursue the matter any further, who knew what trouble these people could bring.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯和威尔伯小心谨慎，坚信任何人都不应该再追究此事，谁知道这些人会带来什么麻烦。

sentences.en: William and Jorge, however, were open to the possibility of an encounter.
sentences.zh: 然而，威廉和豪尔赫对见面的可能性持开放态度。

sentences.en: Within hours of the revelation,
sentences.zh: 在真相大白几小时后，

sentences.en: Janet had arranged for William and Jorge to meet in a public square at nine that evening, soon after William closed up the butcher shop.
sentences.zh: 珍妮就安排威廉和豪尔赫当晚九点在一个公共广场见面，就在威廉打烊肉铺后不久。

sentences.en: Wilbur, initially averse to meeting the other brothers, felt increasingly curious as he looked at the pictures.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯最初排斥与其他兄弟见面，但在看着照片时，好奇心却日渐滋长。

sentences.en: He wanted to go, too.
sentences.zh: 他也想去。

sentences.en: Around 3 p.m.,
sentences.zh: 下午3点左右，

sentences.en: William spoke to Jorge for the first time and asked if he could invite Wilbur, along with Brian and Janet.
sentences.zh: 威廉第一次与豪尔赫通话，询问是否可以邀请威尔伯以及布莱恩和珍妮一同前往。

sentences.en: He was relieved when Jorge said yes.
sentences.zh: 当豪尔赫说可以时，他松了一口气。

sentences.en: Both noticed that their voices did not sound alike.
sentences.zh: 两人都注意到他们的声音听起来并不像。

sentences.en: William's was huskier, and of course, there was the Santander accent.
sentences.zh: 威廉的嗓音更低沉粗犷，当然，还有桑坦德的口音。

sentences.en: William also called
sentences.zh: 威廉也叫

sentences.en: Jorge, sir, a formality typical of people from the countryside.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫“先生”，这是乡下人典型的客套。

sentences.en: Jorge thought he liked this person's voice.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫觉得自己挺喜欢这个人的声音。

sentences.en: He sounded not just nice, but good.
sentences.zh: 他听起来不仅人好，而且声音也动听。

sentences.en: As the hour grew closer,
sentences.zh: 随着时间越来越近，

sentences.en: William went quiet from nerves.
sentences.zh: 威廉紧张得沉默不语。

sentences.en: He took off from work to get a haircut.
sentences.zh: 他请假去剪了头发。

sentences.en: He put on his best sweater, which is black with gray stripes.
sentences.zh: 他穿上了自己最好的毛衣，是一件带有灰色条纹的黑色毛衣。

sentences.en: He strapped on his gun, which he wore as a matter of course ever since he served in the military.
sentences.zh: 他系上了枪套，自从参军以来，他一直随身带着枪，这对他来说是理所当然的事。

sentences.en: He paced.
sentences.zh: 他在原地踱着步。

sentences.en: Across town,
sentences.zh: 城的另一头，

sentences.en: Jorge was also feeling jittery.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫也感到心神不定。

sentences.en: He had asked his brother to go with him, but Carlos had a date he was not willing to cancel.
sentences.zh: 他曾叫他弟弟陪他一起去，但卡洛斯有个约会，不愿取消。

sentences.en: When Jorge ran into a friend from the university, he spontaneously asked him to join him for moral support.
sentences.zh: 当豪尔赫偶遇一位大学朋友时，他脱口而出邀请对方陪他去，好给他打气。

sentences.en: At the appointed time,
sentences.zh: 到了约定好的时间，

sentences.en: Jorge stood in the square, looking around.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫站在广场上，四处张望。

sentences.en: His palms were damp, and he could hardly breathe from the sensation of pressure he felt in his stomach.
sentences.zh: 他的手心直冒汗，胃部传来的压迫感让他几乎喘不过气来。

sentences.en: Within minutes, a group started walking toward him.
sentences.zh: 几分钟内，一群人朝他走了过来。

sentences.en: There was William, with Jorge's face, walking just as Jorge did, with that roll and the funny spread of his feet.
sentences.zh: 威廉出现了，他长着豪尔赫的脸，走路的姿势也和豪尔赫一模一样，带着那种摇晃的步态和双脚外八的滑稽模样。

sentences.en: Brian filmed the encounter on his phone.
sentences.zh: 布莱恩用手机拍摄下了这次相遇。

sentences.en: With the sound turned off, the nervous chatter muted, the video captures
sentences.zh: 在关闭声音、屏蔽了紧张的闲聊之后，这段视频捕捉到了

sentences.en: Jorge and William engaging in what looks like some kind of highly choreographed,
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫和威廉进行着某种看起来高度编排、

sentences.en: ritualized pantomime.
sentences.zh: 仪式化的哑剧表演。

sentences.en: William stares at Jorge as Jorge looks off to the side.
sentences.zh: 威廉凝视着豪尔赫，而豪尔赫则把目光投向一侧。

sentences.en: Then William turns his head away, as if intuitively giving Jorge the chance to stare at his face, which he does, looking him up and down.
sentences.zh: 接着威廉把头转开，仿佛出于直觉般给豪尔赫机会去端详他的脸，豪尔赫也确实照做了，上下打量着他。

sentences.en: The two stare directly at each other.
sentences.zh: 两人四目相对。

sentences.en: There's a moment of eye contact that is shockingly intimate,
sentences.zh: 有那么一瞬间，眼神的交汇亲密得令人震惊，

sentences.en: and an exchange of smiles, and then they each look quickly away.
sentences.zh: 伴随着相视一笑，随后两人又都迅速把目光移开。

sentences.en: As they keep stealing glimpses of each other, they look the way lovers might when they are on the brink of confessing for the first time to a mutual infatuation.
sentences.zh: 当他们不断偷偷瞥向对方时，那神情就像是一对恋人正处于首次向对方坦白暗恋之情的边缘。

sentences.en: Jorge pulls himself together, looks at William a bit more appraisingly.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫收敛心神，带着更多审视的意味看着威廉。

sentences.en: Jorge is chewing gum, and his jaw is working hard.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫在嚼口香糖，他的下巴正使劲嚼着。

sentences.en: He puts his hand on his cheek, pressing his own flesh.
sentences.zh: 他把手放在脸颊上，捏了捏自己的肉。

sentences.en: Yes, this is me.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我。

sentences.en: That person over there, that is him.
sentences.zh: 那边那个人，那就是他。

sentences.en: William is quiet, shifting his weight so that he appears to be swaying from side to side.
sentences.zh: 威廉静静地站着，调整着重心，看起来像是在左右摇晃。

sentences.en: It was like staring through a mirror, and on the other side of the mirror, there's a parallel universe,
sentences.zh: 就像是透过一面镜子凝视，而在镜子的另一边，存在着一个平行宇宙，

sentences.en: Jorge would say later.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫日后这样说道。

sentences.en: It was easier, clearly, for Jorge to turn his gaze to Wilbur, the double of Carlos.
sentences.zh: 显然，对豪尔赫来说，把目光转向卡洛斯的双胞胎威尔伯要更容易些。

sentences.en: Jorge stares at Wilbur and shakes his head.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫凝视着威尔伯，摇了摇头。

sentences.en: Wilbur has seen the photos of Carlos, who wore glasses.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯看过卡洛斯的照片，卡洛斯戴着眼镜。

sentences.en: All I need are the glasses,
sentences.zh: 我只需要一副眼镜就行了，

sentences.en: Wilbur said.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯说道。

sentences.en: He let out a high-pitched giggle, and Jorge felt that pressure in his chest again.
sentences.zh: 他发出了一声高亢的咯咯笑声，豪尔赫感到胸口再次传来了那种压迫感。

sentences.en: That was Carlos' laugh.
sentences.zh: 那是卡洛斯的笑声。

sentences.en: Having seen how much William looked like Jorge,
sentences.zh: 在看到威廉和豪尔赫长得如此相像之后，

sentences.en: Wilbur was now eager to meet Carlos.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯现在急切地想要见见卡洛斯。

sentences.en: Jorge called ahead to say they were coming, and the group piled into two taxis, heading over to Jorge and Carlos' apartment.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫提前打电话说他们要来，一行人挤进两辆出租车，朝豪尔赫和卡洛斯的公寓驶去。

sentences.en: Around ten,
sentences.zh: 大约十点左右，

sentences.en: Carlos heard the doorbell ring.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯听到门铃响了。

sentences.en: He walked to the door, and then stood there, paralyzed.
sentences.zh: 他走到门前，然后僵立在那里。

sentences.en: He could barely bring himself to answer.
sentences.zh: 他几乎鼓不起勇气去开门。

sentences.en: He knew it was Jorge and those men from the photos.
sentences.zh: 他知道门外是豪尔赫和照片里的那些人。

sentences.en: Those people were not just strangers, they were stranger than strangers, players in a story about his life over which he had little control.
sentences.zh: 这些人不仅是陌生人，而且比陌生人还要陌生，他们是他生命中某个故事里的演员，而他对此却几乎无法掌控。

sentences.en: Open the door,
sentences.zh: 开门，

sentences.en: Jorge commanded.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫命令道。

sentences.en: Carlos heard a giggle.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯听到了一声咯咯的笑声。

sentences.en: It was his own, but it was not coming from him.
sentences.zh: 那是他自己的笑声，但并非发自他口。

sentences.en: Or maybe it was.
sentences.zh: 或者也许真的是他。

sentences.en: I don't want to,
sentences.zh: 我不想开，

sentences.en: Carlos said.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯说。

sentences.en: I'm scared.
sentences.zh: 我害怕。

sentences.en: The moments ticked by.
sentences.zh: 时间一分一秒地过去。

sentences.en: Then, too, with Carlos laughing nervously on one side,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，卡洛斯在一边紧张地笑着，

sentences.en: Wilbur laughing on the other.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯则在另一边笑着。

sentences.en: Carlos, open it,
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯，开门，

sentences.en: Jorge told him again.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫再次对他说。

sentences.en: You cannot block the sun with one finger, their mother used to say.
sentences.zh: 他们以前的母亲常说，欲盖弥彰。

sentences.en: Carlos opened the door, and the group filed in, like a procession from a dream.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯打开了门，众人鱼贯而入，就像梦境中的游行队伍一样。

sentences.en: There was Jorge, and there was his double.
sentences.zh: 那是豪尔赫，还有他的双胞胎替身。

sentences.en: It was Jorge in a strange sweater.
sentences.zh: 那是穿着奇怪毛衣的豪尔赫。

sentences.en: Jorge, only quiet.
sentences.zh: 只是变安静了的豪尔赫。

sentences.en: Jorge, without the cool confidence.
sentences.zh: 失去了那种酷劲和自信的豪尔赫。

sentences.en: There was some woman, and some other guy, and then there was,
sentences.zh: 那里有个女人，还有另一个家伙，然后还有，

sentences.en: Carlos was staring at himself, an altered version of himself, a funny photocopy, a joke, a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯正凝视着自己，一个被魔改的自己，一份滑稽的复印件，一个笑话，一场噩梦。

sentences.en: Carlos looked at Wilbur, his mirror image.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯看着威尔伯，也就是他的镜像。

sentences.en: They took a quick peek at each other.
sentences.zh: 他们飞快地看了对方一眼。

sentences.en: They both shouted, aye!
sentences.zh: 两人同时大喊：哎呀！

sentences.en: and turned their backs, covering their eyes, each turning red.
sentences.zh: 然后转过身去，捂住眼睛，两人的脸都红了。

sentences.en: Wilbur started speaking, but Carlos was having a hard time catching what he was saying.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯开始说话，但卡洛斯很难听清他在说些什么。

sentences.en: Instead of rolling his R's,
sentences.zh: 威尔伯没有发出颤音R，

sentences.en: Wilbur spoke with hard D's, the speech impediment.
sentences.zh: 而是用生硬的D音说话，这是一种语言障碍。

sentences.en: Carlos had had one as a child, but overcame it with speech therapy.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯小时候也有过这种障碍，但通过语言治疗克服了。

sentences.en: All four started comparing notes, quizzing one another, finding out which essential qualities the identical twins shared.
sentences.zh: 四个人开始核对情况、互相盘问，找出这几对同卵双胞胎拥有哪些共同的本质特征。

sentences.en: Who were the crybabies of the family?
sentences.zh: 谁是家里的爱哭鬼？

sentences.en: Carlos and Wilbur.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯和威尔伯。

sentences.en: Who had sweet temperaments?
sentences.zh: 谁的脾气最好？

sentences.en: Jorge and William.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫和威廉。

sentences.en: Who were more organized?
sentences.zh: 谁更有条理？

sentences.en: Carlos and Wilbur.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯和威尔伯。

sentences.en: Who were the girl chasers?
sentences.zh: 谁更喜欢追女孩？

sentences.en: Carlos and Wilbur.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯和威尔伯。

sentences.en: Who were the strongest?
sentences.zh: 谁力气最大？

sentences.en: Jorge and William.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫和威廉。

sentences.en: Even still, while Jorge was seeing sameness with every glance he stole at William,
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，豪尔赫每次偷看威廉时都能看到相同之处，

sentences.en: Carlos was seeking differences between him and his country double.
sentences.zh: 而卡洛斯则在寻找自己与乡村双胞胎兄弟之间的不同点。

sentences.en: Look at our hands,
sentences.zh: 看看我们的手，

sentences.en: Carlos said.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯说。

sentences.en: They're not the same.
sentences.zh: 它们不一样。

sentences.en: Wilbur's were bigger, more swollen, marked with scars from countless quarrels with the knives of the butcher shop and the machetes he used in the fields growing up.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯的手更大、更肿胀，上面布满了伤痕，那是他在肉铺切肉时与刀具无数次争斗以及在田间长大时使用大砍刀留下的印记。

sentences.en: Carlos, by contrast, frequently got manicures.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，卡洛斯经常做美甲。

sentences.en: His nails, as is not uncommon among male professionals in Colombia, were covered in clear gloss.
sentences.zh: 跟哥伦比亚的许多职业男性一样，他的指甲涂了一层透明亮油。

sentences.en: William asked Jorge about Jorge's biological mother.
sentences.zh: 威廉向豪尔赫打听豪尔赫的亲生母亲。

sentences.en: How was she?
sentences.zh: 她怎么样？

sentences.en: Where was she?
sentences.zh: 她在哪里？

sentences.en: Watching William's face carefully,
sentences.zh: 仔细观察着威廉的脸，

sentences.en: Jorge told him that their mother died of cancer four years before.
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫告诉他，他们的母亲四年前死于癌症。

sentences.en: He showed him a photo of her as a young woman.
sentences.zh: 他向他展示了一张她年轻时的照片。

sentences.en: Long hair clipped back, beautiful eyes set in a kind, and serious face.
sentences.zh: 长发往后别着，慈祥而严肃的脸上嵌着一双美丽的眼睛。

sentences.en: Staring at the photo,
sentences.zh: 凝视着这张照片，

sentences.en: William was struck with a new blow of grief.
sentences.zh: 威廉遭受了又一次沉重的悲痛打击。

sentences.zh: 在开始研究之前，如果每个年轻人的测试结果都与他的同卵双胞胎相似，西格尔并不会感到惊讶，尽管他们的环境不同。

sentences.en: But her preliminary results, she said, show that on a number of traits, the identical twins were less alike than she initially anticipated.
sentences.zh: 但她说，她的初步结果表明，在许多特征上，同卵双胞胎并不像她最初预期的那样相似。

sentences.en: I came away with a real respect for the effect of an extremely different environment, Siegel said.
sentences.zh: 西格尔说，我对极端不同环境所产生的影响产生了真正的敬意。

sentences.en: Perhaps the results merely indicate that people raised in deeply rural environments with little education take tests in a wholly different manner from
sentences.zh: 也许这些结果只是表明，在受教育程度很低的极度农村环境中长大的人，其参加测试的方式与

sentences.en: those who attend a university.
sentences.zh: 上大学的人完全不同。

sentences.en: William, who managed a small business with competence, at times seemed overwhelmed by the teSt. But Siegel considered the young men's story a case
sentences.zh: 威廉能胜任地管理一家小企业，有时却会被测试压得喘不过气来。但西格尔认为，这几位年轻人的故事是一个案例

sentences.en: history that might provoke further research, inspiring others to seek out more examples of twins reared apart with significantly different upbringings, whatever they were.
sentences.zh: 史，可能会引发进一步的研究，激励其他人去寻找更多在显著不同的成长经历下分开抚养的双胞胎的例子，无论他们的经历是什么。

sentences.en: Over the course of the week that the young men spent on Siegel's questionnaires, they looked back at the past that helped make them who they were.
sentences.zh: 在年轻人填写西格尔问卷的一个星期里，他们回顾了塑造他们今天的自我的过去。

sentences.en: How many books did they have in their childhood homes?
sentences.zh: 他们童年的家里有多少本书？

sentences.en: Did they ever smoke?
sentences.zh: 他们抽过烟吗？

sentences.en: Did they grow up in families in which people kept their feelings to themselves?
sentences.zh: 他们是在那种人们把感情藏在心里的家庭里长大的吗？

sentences.en: For one week, they stepped out of time to look backward.
sentences.zh: 整整一个星期，他们脱离了时间的轨迹去回顾过去。

sentences.en: But the moment Siegel would leave, they would continue on their usual paths, speeding forward towards some unknown future, colliding with chance.
sentences.zh: 但只要西格尔一离开，他们就会继续他们寻常的道路，朝着某种未知的未来飞奔，与机遇狭路相逢。

sentences.en: They sometimes talked about all living together.
sentences.zh: 他们有时会谈论住在一起的事。

sentences.en: As four, William liked to think, they were at their strongeSt. Like members of any family, they might drift and then regroup, or find themselves falling back on the deep comfort of
sentences.zh: 威廉喜欢认为，他们四个人在一起时是最强大的。就像任何家庭的成员一样，他们可能会漂泊然后重新集结，或者发现自己重新依赖起

sentences.en: their particular bonds.
sentences.zh: 他们独特的纽带所带来的深深安慰。

sentences.en: It is rare to grow up as a twin at all, part of a primal pair.
sentences.zh: 作为双胞胎长大事实上很罕见，这是一对原始双子星的一部分。

sentences.en: Now each young man had a second rare pairing, a second chance at an unusual kind of closeness.
sentences.zh: 现在每个年轻人都有了第二种罕见的配对，有了第二次获得不寻常亲密感的机会。

sentences.en: What did that kind of entanglement, a double-doubling, mean for whom they would each become, or what they might achieve?
sentences.zh: 这种纠缠，即双重加倍，对于他们每个人将成为什么样的人，或者他们可能会取得什么成就意味着什么？

sentences.en: To celebrate the end of a week's worth of research, Siegel and Montoya decided to take the young men dancing one night at a popular Bogota steakhouse with a big dance floor.
sentences.zh: 为了庆祝长达一周的研究结束，西格尔和蒙托亚决定有一天晚上带年轻人去波哥大一家带大型舞池的知名牛排馆跳舞。

sentences.en: Jorge and
sentences.zh: 豪尔赫和

sentences.en: William took turns dancing with Siegel.
sentences.zh: 威廉轮流和西格尔跳舞。

sentences.en: They smiled gamely and turned and twirled, with only glancing attention to the rhythm.
sentences.zh: 他们大方地微笑着，旋转着，对节拍只是草草应付。

sentences.en: Carlos, in his element, showed Wilbur a few steps.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯如鱼得水，向威尔伯展示了几个舞步。

sentences.en: They danced in not quite synchrony, side by side, Carlos with sureness, Wilbur staring down at his feet and concentrating.
sentences.zh: 他们跳舞并不完全同步，并肩而立，卡洛斯信心十足，而威尔伯则盯着自己的脚全神贯注。

sentences.en: Occasionally he looked up, as if he was feeling it.
sentences.zh: 他偶尔抬起头，好像他正在领会其中的感觉。

sentences.en: He would get the hang of it soon enough, he knew.
sentences.zh: 他知道自己很快就会掌握要领的。

sentences.en: Wilbur has the goods, Montoya said, watching from the table.
sentences.zh: 蒙托亚在桌旁看着说，威尔伯很有天赋。

sentences.en: He just needs the experience.
sentences.zh: 他只是需要经验。

sentences.en: When all the brothers stopped for more aguardiente, a sugarcane-based liqueur, and sat at the table, they took turns flirting with a young woman who had joined the party.
sentences.zh: 当所有兄弟停下来喝更多的阿瓜迪恩特（一种以甘蔗为原料的利口酒）并在桌旁坐下时，他们轮流调戏一个加入聚会的年轻女子。

sentences.en: Here at the club, Carlos was assured, poised, smooth.
sentences.zh: 在这里的俱乐部里，卡洛斯自信、镇定、圆滑。

sentences.en: As the evening wore on, and he drank more aguardiente, his moves got bigger, more daring, until he was showing off a maneuver that he and a friend had made up one night,
sentences.zh: 随着夜色渐深，他喝了更多的阿瓜迪恩特，他的动作变得更大、更大胆，直到他开始炫耀一个他和朋友某天晚上自创的动作，

sentences.en: a pivot from the waist that had him leaning so far back that his spine was practically parallel with the floor, his knees bent and nearly buckling.
sentences.zh: 一个从腰部开始的旋转动作，这使他向后仰得如此之远，以至于他的脊椎几乎与地板平行，膝盖弯曲且几乎要瘫软。

sentences.en: Carlos called that move the
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯将这个动作称为

sentences.en: Matrix, after a similar backward dodge that the movie's star, Keanu Reeves, executes while evading bullets in a parallel universe.
sentences.zh: 黑客帝国，这是模仿电影主角基努·里维斯在平行宇宙中躲避子弹时执行的类似后仰闪避动作。

sentences.en: As he leaned all the way back, Carlos looked as if he might lose his balance altogether.
sentences.zh: 当他一路向后倾斜时，卡洛斯看起来甚至快要失去平衡了。

sentences.en: Wilbur, William, and Jorge quickly surrounded him, still dancing, a mixture of emotions on their faces.
sentences.zh: 威尔伯、威廉和豪尔赫迅速围在他周围，依然跳着舞，他们的脸上交织着各种情绪。

sentences.en: Amusement, irritation, concern.
sentences.zh: 娱乐、恼怒、担忧。

sentences.en: But Carlos was not falling.
sentences.zh: 但卡洛斯并没有摔倒。

sentences.en: It only looked that way, and he managed to right himself.
sentences.zh: 看起来是那样而已，他设法调整好了身形。

sentences.en: The dancing went on as before.
sentences.zh: 舞蹈照常进行。

sentences.en: The four men seemed to bounce off one another in different pairs and groupings, splitting off in
sentences.zh: 这四个男人似乎在不同的舞伴和组合中互相弹开，分散开来

sentences.en: search of young women returning to compare notes before heading out onto the floor again.
sentences.zh: 寻找年轻女子，在再次步入舞池前返回交流心得。

sentences.en: They were one, they were two, they were four, merging, dividing, and merging again as the music played long into the evening.
sentences.zh: 随着音乐在深夜里久久回荡，他们是一体，是两人，是四人，融合、分裂，然后再次融合。
